name: Right-Wing Populism
summary: Right-wing populism, in the scholarship on the populist radical right, is populism (a pure people against a corrupt elite, politics as the people's general will, impatience with institutions that constrain it) joined to nativism, the demand that the nation be made up of its natives, and to authoritarianism. The defining scholarship names this core and little else, so most economic, social and foreign-policy positions vary between parties and are not part of the ideology.
scope: The populist radical right as Cas Mudde and Cristobal Rovira Kaltwasser define it: a core ideology that combines nativism, authoritarianism and populism, found in Europe (Fidesz, the Austrian Freedom Party) and elsewhere. Positions that parties of the family differ on, or that only a leader's speeches or a party's platform state, are not part of the ideology and are left null. Left-wing populism, historical agrarian populism and the broader populism are other subjects.
